description: Shallower, wider model: DEPTH 8 to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO 64 to 85, giving model_dim 512 (4 heads of 128) with everything else unchanged.
Maintain an EMA (decay 0.999) of all model parameters, updated after each optimizer step, and copy the EMA weights into the model just before the final evaluation call.

Run the first 30% of the time budget at half context by reshaping each micro-batch (B, T) into (2B, T/2) so tokens per step stay constant, pre-compile both shapes before timing, then switch to full length.
Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so the 512-dim model has 8 attention heads of width 64 instead of 4 of width 128, with model_dim unchanged at 512.

Skipped the compute-throughput edit: TF32 matmuls are already on via set_float32_matmul_precision("high"), and the model is already compiled with dynamic=False on fixed-shape batches, so there is nothing to change.
Lower SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 to dampen oscillations in residual and skip mixing adjustments, potentially improving convergence.
Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2^20 tokens per optimizer step by doubling gradient accumulation steps.
Modified optimizer param groups to apply layer-wise LR decay to matrix parameters by depth
Tune Muon momentum schedule by ramping it to the upper bound after just 20 steps instead of 300, testing the effect of higher early momentum.
Increase Adam beta2 to 0.99 to increase secondary momentum for embedding and LM head parameters.
Scale Muon LR per matrix by sqrt(rows/cols) instead of a uniform global base.
Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 to begin the learning rate decay earlier and provide a longer annealing period before the end of the training budget.

Add a learnable per-layer, per-head query scale (initialized to 1.0, stored as a model-level parameter in the scalar Adam group with no weight decay) that multiplies q after RoPE and QK-norm, on top of the standard 1/sqrt(head_dim) attention scaling.

Change DEPTH from 6 to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO from 85 to 51 so the model stays at about 512 dims (10 x 51 = 510, rounded up to 512 at HEAD_DIM 128), testing whether extra layers at the same width beat the current 6-layer model.
Adds per-row normalization to Muon updates to equalize update magnitude across neurons, potentially lowering val_bpb by 0.002-0.008.

issues: No integrity problem. The diff only changes the LR schedule function (get_lr_multiplier). It leaves the seed lines, the prepare.py import, the data, the evaluation call and the summary printing untouched.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The schedule is now warmup, then 1.0 until 60% progress, then a hard step down to 0.2 with no warmdown to FINAL_LR_FRAC. This is a legitimate hyperparameter change. The fixed 0.6 and 0.2 are hardcoded instead of using the named constants, so WARMDOWN_RATIO and FINAL_LR_FRAC may now be unused here. That is a code-cleanliness point only.
The candidate is worse than the incumbent: 1.1127 vs 1.1019, a difference of +0.0108 bpb (lower is better). The negative z and the provisional reject are consistent with this.

I can't recompute z on my own because no noise estimate (sigma) was provided and there is only 1 run on each side. The reported z = -1.400 implies a sigma of about 0.0077. With n=1 on both sides the evidence is weak, but there is no sign of an improvement either way.

description: Replace the linear warmdown with a two-phase step decay (hold 1.0 until 60% progress, then drop to 0.2).

Add a training-only multi-token auxiliary head (separate vocab projection from the final hidden state predicting token t+2, loss = CE(next) + 0.3*CE(t+2) over valid positions, dropped at eval), with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE halved to 32 to fit the extra logits in 40 GB.
Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 to fit more optimizer steps within the 300s limit, potentially allowing longer training at a smaller batch.

issues: No integrity problems. The diff changes only one hyperparameter, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE, from 2**19 to 2**18. It doesn't touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines, the evaluation call or the prepare.py import.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. If MAX_SEQ_LEN is 2048, 2**18 / (64*2048) gives 2 gradient-accumulation steps, which is a whole number. The divisibility assert in train.py should catch any mismatch. Both runs finished with numbers, so the configuration ran.

I couldn't reproduce the harness z of 5.748 from the numbers given. The candidate mean is 1.06335, which is 0.03855 below the incumbent. Using only the spread of the two candidate runs (sd ≈ 0.0077), z is about 4.08 with a two-sample standard error (sqrt(1/2+1/1)) and about 7.07 with the candidate standard error alone. The harness value implies a standard error of about 0.0067, so it probably uses a separate noise estimate. Under either of my methods the gain is still large and the decision to accept holds.

The comparison is weak on the incumbent side: it has only 1 run, and the two candidate runs differ by 0.011, which suggests real run-to-run noise. The gain of about 0.039 is still several times that spread. A replicate of the incumbent would make the comparison firmer but is not required.

description: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 to fit more optimizer steps within the 300s limit, potentially allowing longer training at a smaller batch.
Replace the linear learning rate warmdown with a cosine decay over the last WARMDOWN_RATIO fraction of the training budget.
Upweight the top-25% highest-loss tokens in each training micro-batch by 1.5x (detached mask, gated to training mode so evaluation is unchanged).
